chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave girl who was under a slave [husband], so the slave girl was emancipated. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her command is in her hands; if she wishes, she keeps herself with her husband, and if she wishes, she removes herself from him.'

And he mentioned that Barirah was with a husband of hers, and she was an owned slave. So Ayesha bought her and emancipated her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave her a choice and said: 'If she wishes, she stays with her husband, and if she wishes, she separates from him.' And it was so that her masters, who had sold her, had stipulated upon Ayesha that their mastership would be for her. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The mastership is for the one who emancipates.'

And meat was given in charity to Barirah, so she gifted it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So Ayesha kept it aside and said, 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) does not eat the meat of charity.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came, and the meat was kept aside, so he said: 'What is the matter with this meat not having been cooked?' So she said, 'O Messenger of Allah! It was given in charity to Barirah, and you do not eat the charity.' So he said: 'It is charity for her, and for us it is a gift.' Then he ordered with cooking it. Thus, there flowed three Sunnahs in it.'

key_terms.أَمْرُهَا بِيَدِهَا: Her command/choice is in her hands
key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah (the slave woman whose case set the precedent)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave woman's marriage if she is emancipated while her husband remains a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ikhtiyar' (choice) for a freed slave woman, illustrating how manumission can dissolve the marital bond if she chooses, as seen in the precedent of Barirah. It further clarifies the legal distinction between 'walayah' (right of manumission) and 'sadaqah' (charity), noting that the Prophet accepted Barirah's gift by reclassifying it as a 'hadiyah' to avoid the prohibition of consuming charity. This narrative underscores the Prophet's practical wisdom in navigating social customs while maintaining strict legal boundaries regarding property and status.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a slave girl who was under a slave, so the slave girl was emancipated. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Her command is in her hands. If she so desires to she leaves herself with her husband, and if she so desires to she removes herself from him’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that Bureyra was with a husband of hers, and she was an owned slave. So Ayesha bought her and emancipated her. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> gave her a choice and said: ‘If she so desires to she stays with her husband, and if she so desires to, she separates from him’; and it was so that her masters who had sold her had stipulated upon Ayesha that her mastership would be for them. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The mastership is for the one who emancipates’.

And some meat was given in charity to Bureyra, so she gifted it to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So Ayesha kept it aside and said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> does not eat the charity’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> came over and the meat was kept aside, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with this meat not having been cooked?’ So she said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! It was given in charity with upon Bureyra and you<sup>saww</sup> do not eat the charity’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is a charity for her, and for us<sup>saww</sup> it is a gift’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> ordered with cooking it. Thus, there flowed three Sunnahs in it’.
